sections.heading: B — Audience, Sharing the road
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, Sharing the road

The audience is first-time, never-licensed applicants for a Michigan operator's license, reading at a plain-English level, plus newcomers and parents of teen drivers who use the same handbook. This section covers commercial vehicles with their stopping distances, no zones and wide turns, passing trucks safely, slow-moving vehicles and horse-drawn buggies, pedestrians including those with white canes or guide dogs, children, motorcycles, scooters and mopeds, bicyclists with the passing distance law, and autocycles. It teaches how to drive safely around trucks, slow vehicles, pedestrians and riders, and the specific Michigan rules for passing motorcycles and bicyclists. It assumes no prior driving knowledge and no prerequisites beyond literacy, so wording stays concrete, procedural and free of legal jargon throughout.
